guitar.modelsText: Gibson SG / Fender Telecaster / Gibson Les Paul
guitar.notes: Confirmed — Louis Bertignac is well known in French rock for SG and Telecaster usage; medium confidence appropriate given two guitarists and varied gear.

tone.target: bright French rock crunch with bite
tone.profile: bright French rock crunch with bite
tone.summary: A tight signal chain using a Boost/OD for bite, followed by an AC30 style amp and UK Vintage 4x12 cab to achieve the required Plexi-esque French rock sound.

rig.name: Téléphone - Au Coeur De La Nuit - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and tighten the rhythm playing.
Provide the necessary tight overdrive and mid-forward bite (like a boost pedal).
Simulate the classic Plexi/British crunch tone and add slight grit.
Provide the core British rock sound and forward mids required for anthemic rhythm.
Match the Marshall/Plexi style and provide a classic British cabinet sound.
Fine-tune the frequency response to emphasize forward mids and bite.
Add a subtle, non-washy ambience (small room) without sounding like large hall reverb.
Optional subtle rhythmic delay for anthemic feel (kept off by default).
blocks.gap: The verdict suggests dropping big delays, so this is optional and set to inactive.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism and mid-range focus by swapping the current IR for a more aggressive, vintage 4x12 model.

proposals.reason: Enhance the bite and vintage character required for French rock crunch.
